items.title: Valuation bounds in a quasi-finite extension of a one-dimensional local domain, with equality exactly in the finite case
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a finite type extension of a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain with finite fraction field extension is semi-local, and bounds the order of an element times the degree by a sum of local orders weighted by residue field degrees, with equality exactly when the extension is finite (statement lines 31180-31202). The proof does not compute the orders directly: it passes to a finite subalgebra of the integral closure agreeing with the extension away from the maximal ideals, compares the two sides through the indices of that subalgebra, and detects finiteness by exhibiting an ideal of denominators which lies in no maximal ideal (proof lines 31204-31233). The comparison through the finite subalgebra is the step carrying the estimate. H2.
